audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] says 'even with Realm Warp unlocked' at the Levels 4-5 row — Realm Warp is his level 6 ultimate — and whys[5]/whys[6] claim you stay ahead through both item stages while spikes[2] and spikes[3] say the opposite.
audit.why: Realm Warp (R, 180/160/140s, 3000 range) does no damage at all; it is a portal. The real stage shift is first item, where Tear-line mana feeds his passive and Overload resets off every other cast.
audit.corrected: Level 6 = a 180s damage-free portal, so the duel is still yours; First item = his mana scaling arrives; 2+ items = Flux-fed root chains are his phase.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rune Prison is called a root everywhere with no mention of the condition on it, and Comeuppance is described as global twice.
audit.why: Rune Prison (W, 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, 615 range) only SLOWS unless the target already has Flux from Spell Flux (E, 3.5/3.25/3/2.75/2.5s, 615 range) — dodging the orb downgrades the whole lockdown. Overload (Q, flat 5s, 1000 range) is reset by his other basic abilities, so counting it as a 5-second cooldown overestimates your safety. Comeuppance is 2500 range, not global, and it stops on the first champion, minion or structure it hits.
audit.corrected: Sidestep Spell Flux and Rune Prison is only a slow you can walk out of. Both of his lockdown tools reach 615 units while your Q reaches 850 — that gap is the lane. Comeuppance covers 2500 units and needs a clean line, so fire it at a fleeing Ryze, not across the map.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers, and the advice implies waiting out Overload.
audit.why: Overload is a flat 5s and resets off his other casts, so it is never the window. Rune Prison at 11s rank 1 is.
audit.corrected: Step up in the 11 seconds after Rune Prison; never plan around Overload's cooldown, because his other spells reset it.
